complexity.notes: Clean and readable recursion; the `bool(p) ^ bool(q)` mismatch check is a slightly cute but correct idiom. Recursion depth is bounded by tree height, O(n) in the degenerate case, which could hit Python's recursion limit for very large skewed trees.
complexity.summary: For each node of root, recursively compare the subtree rooted there against subRoot with a standard same-tree check; returns true on the first match. The generalized worst case (e.g., two long chains of equal values) forces a full O(m) comparison at most of the n nodes, giving O(n*m), which becomes O(n^2) when both trees scale with n.
